facts.text: Cover: 'Determining the Effectiveness of Stairwell Pressurization Systems in Multi-Story Buildings', J. Cheong, ENFE 682 (2017), Department of Civil and Natural Resources Engineering, University of Canterbury; supervisor named on the cover.

facts.text: Abstract: a ten-storey building with a stairwell pressurisation system 'was designed according to' AS/NZS 1668.1:2015 and was then modelled in Fire Dynamic Simulator (FDS).
facts.locator: UC student study (10 pp), PDF p.1

facts.text: Abstract findings: the fire floor 'could not rely solely on building leakage' and needed a relief vent; the stairwell also needed a pressure relief vent for over-pressurisation; the system works as intended only if the building is designed on phased evacuation and the fire-floor stair door shuts after that floor is evacuated.
facts.locator: UC student study (10 pp), PDF p.1

facts.text: Introduction cites NZBC Clause C4 (means of escape) as the functional requirement.
facts.locator: UC student study (10 pp), PDF p.1

facts.text: Objective: determine the effectiveness of a pressurised stairwell designed in FDS to AS/NZS 1668.1:2015, with scenarios taken from Section 10.3.
facts.locator: UC student study (10 pp), PDF p.2

facts.text: An office occupancy was chosen as a common multi-storey occupancy. Fire-alarm systems modelled (smoke detection and sprinkler) are 'based on' NZBC Clause F7.
facts.locator: UC student study (10 pp), PDF p.2
